transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... I just don't really feel like myself lately. I don't know. I barely talk to anyone anymore. I just sort of go... flat, I guess. Quiet. It's just getting hard to do things. Even just getting started on my cleaning route at work... it feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
A while, I guess. ...Maybe a year and two months. Give or take. It started... well, not long after I moved.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No... not really. I don't think I've ever felt like that. Just mostly tired, I guess.
Over this past year or so, has your low mood and low energy been present almost every day without a break, or have there been stretches of weeks where you felt back to your normal self?

I don't know... it's just always there, I guess. Most of the time since I moved. The... the sadness and the low energy. Even when other things are happening... like when I'm worried about the cameras, or when the voices are louder... the tired feeling is still just... there in the background. It doesn't really go away.
Do the voices and worries about the cameras happen only when you're feeling down and low on energy, or do they also occur at times when your mood feels okay?

I suppose... well, there was a stretch of a few weeks where it wasn't quite as heavy. I was getting through my shifts at the building a little easier... eating my meals alright. 

But... no, the other stuff didn't stop. I still heard my name echoing in the stairwell. And... I just knew those hallway cameras were still being used to track me. So... yeah. It happens anyway.
Have you noticed any other physical changes during this time, like unexplained weight gain, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or hair thinning?
I don't think so. No. Just... no real changes like that.
During that few-week stretch when your mood and energy felt better, were the voices and worries about the cameras still just as strong and frequent as usual?

Yeah... like I said a minute ago. Even when my mood lifted some and getting through my shifts was a bit easier, the other stuff didn't let up. I still heard my name down in the stairwell just the same. And I... I was still sure about those cameras tracking me. It didn't change.
Has there ever been a period of two weeks or more where you experienced the voices or the feeling about the cameras, but you did NOT have any low mood, low energy, or sadness at all during that time?

I... I feel like I just answered that. Yes. 

It was a stretch of several weeks. My mood had lifted. I wasn't feeling sad... I was getting through my work and my meals better. But... I still heard my name in the stairwell. And I stayed convinced about the cameras tracking me. So... yes. Several weeks.

It was... the depression part started first, I think. It's been with me for about a year and two months now. Started not long after I moved. The other things... the voices and the cameras... they came later.
About how long ago did the voices and the worries about the cameras first start—roughly how many months after your low mood began?
I guess... it's been about 11 months now. For the voices and... worrying about being watched.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs regularly during this past year or so?
No. I don't use any of that.

I guess so, yeah. Mostly. Since I moved, the... the sadness and low energy... feeling guilty, not really caring about things... it's just been there. Most of the time. Even if I'm mostly worried about the cameras or the voices... the feeling down is still just... in the background.
During this past year, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
Not really. I just... I sleep about the same as always, I guess. I haven't noticed anything.
During this past year, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or found it hard to concentrate, even during the times when the voices or camera worries were happening?

Yeah, I guess. I used to... I liked fishing on Saturdays. Doing the crossword in the paper with my coffee. Even at work, showing the new guys how to strip a floor right. But... I don't know. I just let it all sit now. It doesn't... it doesn't give me anything back anymore. So I just don't do it.
